settings.repere: Titre H2 · Collagen keeps your skin dewy, bones and
settings.text: Collagen keeps your skin dewy, bones and nails strong, <br class="desktop">and joints creak-free… until it doesn’t.

Line graph showing collagen levels decreasing with age. Collagen remains high until about age 20, then declines steadily, reaching low levels by age 80. A note points to age 20, stating collagen begins to decline in our 20s.

settings.repere: Paragraphe · Your body struggles to replace the colla
settings.text: Your body struggles to replace the collagen you’re losing as quickly as it's breaking down, starting from your 20s. As a result, you lose, on average, 1% of your collagen yearly.

settings.repere: Titre H2 · Two things behind this decline

settings.text: A mature woman with fair skin and gray hair pulled back smiles gently at the camera, posing with one shoulder bare against a soft beige background.

settings.repere: Titre H3 · The natural aging process
Paragraphe · Like all cells in your body, collagen-pr
settings.text: Like all cells in your body, collagen-producing cells (like fibroblasts in the skin and chondrocytes in the cartilage) accumulate DNA damage with age.

settings.repere: Paragraphe · That means the older you get, the fewer
settings.text: That means the older you get, the fewer optimally functioning collagen-producing cells you’ll have in the body, naturally decreasing your collagen levels.
